{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)-5y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=5x(t)-2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=-2\pm 5\text{i},$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1,2}=[\pm \text{i},1]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

For example, when ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=0,$ we obtain the following curve:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x={{field-1}} \\ y={{field-2}}\end{aligned}
$$

worked_solution:
The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

For example, when ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=0,$ we obtain the following curve:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x={e}^{-2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ y={e}^{-2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the coordinates (rounded to two decimal places) of several points on the curve, we get the table below.

| $t$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{20}$ | $\frac{\pi }{10}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $1$ | $0.52$ | $0$ |
| $y$ | $0$ | $0.52$ | $0.53$ |

Let's sketch this solution in the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069757/assets/2b273edc4f977f2bee4d9a8c41128d4f2071ec39b0840610cbb7ee44492aae3e.png)

Notice that $|\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)|\le 1,$ $|\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)|\le 1,$ and ${e}^{-2t}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty .$ Thus, the curve $\text{converges}$ as $t\to \infty .$ So, we have $\text{a spiral}$ that is traversed $\text{counterclockwise}.$

Again, since ${e}^{-2t}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty ,$ the spiral is traversed toward $\text{the origin}$ as $t\to \infty .$

The $\text{phase portrait}$ of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069757/assets/c001f8a99c09e3d1da8c6107a298989c03e64ec58c23319ce0837a757c5ddafd.png)
